name: @arkkvm/arkkvm-mcp

tools.name: device_capabilities
tools.description: Return the capabilities and control boundary of this local ArkKVM MCP adapter. The adapter runs on the controller machine and reaches the ArkKVM device over one of two transports: direct device connection (LAN/VPN, the default) or cloud relay (cloudUrl + cloudToken + cloudDeviceId configured; for devices already adopted by the ArkKVM cloud, reachable over the public internet). Both use WebRTC media plus DataChannels. It exposes device status, read-only device RPC, a device health snapshot, HID control-lease tools (get/request/deny/release) for human/agent arbitration, HDMI screenshots, local HDMI OCR, model-free frame comparison and text waiting, USB HID keyboard/mouse/wheel input plus named key sequences, USB/host IP port forwarding, and the OS-install flow tools: virtual media mount/unmount, storage image upload/delete, and ATX power actions on the controlled machine. The controlled machine is operated only through ArkKVM: this adapter never opens a direct network connection to it. OCR runs locally on the controller against decoded HDMI frames. WebRTC disconnects are not auto-retried; tools return CONNECTION_LOST/CONNECTION_FAILED and the Agent decides whether to call again.

tools.name: device_status
tools.description: Read the ArkKVM device setup status over the configured device URL, plus the local WebRTC session snapshot (state/generation/channel readiness). Use this to verify that ARKKVM_URL points to the KVM device and that the device is initialized. HTTP status reports the KVM device only; connection reflects this MCP process WebRTC control plane (idle until a WebRTC tool has connected). Failures return structured errors: DEVICE_NOT_CONFIGURED, DEVICE_AUTH_REQUIRED, CONNECTION_* when applicable.

tools.name: hdmi_frame_compare
tools.description: Capture two HDMI screenshots separated by a delay and compare them with a model-free grayscale pixel-difference algorithm. Use this to measure whether the controlled screen changed after an input action. It returns both PNG frames, a normalized change score, mean grayscale difference, changed-pixel counts, and approximate changed regions. The result does not identify text, applications, dialogs, buttons, success, or failure; the calling AI agent may inspect the returned image. This tool consumes only the ArkKVM HDMI WebRTC video track and does not send HID input.

delayMs.description: Milliseconds between the two HDMI captures. Default is 500.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum wait for each decoded HDMI frame. Default is 60000; the first capture in a fresh MCP process takes a few seconds while the device emits its next keyframe to the agent session.

threshold.description: Fraction of pixels in the selected region that must differ by at least 16 grayscale levels to report changed. Must be greater than 0; default is 0.03.

region.description: Optional screen region in source HDMI pixels. Omit to compare the full frame.

tools.name: hdmi_ocr
tools.description: Capture one current screenshot from the HDMI-connected controlled machine and convert it to text on the controller machine. The ArkKVM device only supplies the H.264 HDMI video; OCR is performed locally using the command configured by ARKKVM_OCR_COMMAND, which defaults to tesseract. This does not inspect the controller desktop or use a direct connection to the controlled machine.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum time to wait for a decodable HDMI frame in milliseconds. Default is 60000; the first capture in a fresh MCP process takes a few seconds while the device emits its next keyframe to the agent session.

language.description: OCR language data name, for example eng, chi_sim, or eng+chi_sim. Default is ARKKVM_OCR_LANG or eng+chi_sim.

psm.description: Tesseract page segmentation mode. Default is 6.

tools.name: hdmi_ocr_stream
tools.description: Sample the HDMI video for a short time and convert each sampled frame to text on the controller machine. The returned events contain only text changes, in chronological order. This is a bounded MCP operation, not a long-lived network stream; use durationMs and intervalMs to control its sampling window.

durationMs.description: Total OCR sampling window in milliseconds. Default is 5000.

intervalMs.description: Delay between OCR samples in milliseconds. Default is 1000.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum time to wait for a decodable HDMI frame in milliseconds. Default is 60000; the first capture in a fresh MCP process takes a few seconds while the device emits its next keyframe to the agent session.

language.description: OCR language data name. Default is ARKKVM_OCR_LANG or eng+chi_sim.

psm.description: Tesseract page segmentation mode. Default is 6.

tools.name: hdmi_screenshot
tools.description: Capture one current screenshot from the HDMI-connected controlled machine. The ArkKVM device receives HDMI and sends H.264 video over the existing WebRTC media track; this tool receives and decodes one frame on the controller machine, then returns a PNG image for visual inspection or AI analysis. It does not capture the controller desktop or the MCP Inspector page. Use this after device connectivity is available. A successful return means a video frame was decoded, but the image content itself must be inspected to determine what is displayed. If it times out, check HDMI signal/video state and retry. This tool consumes only the HDMI video track and does not send HID input.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum time to wait for a decodable HDMI frame in milliseconds. Default is 60000; the first capture in a fresh MCP process takes a few seconds while the device emits its next keyframe to the agent session.

tools.name: hdmi_video_monitor
tools.description: Monitor the HDMI video stream continuously for a short period using one persistent H.264 decoder. This is the high-frequency, model-free alternative to repeated hdmi_screenshot calls: it consumes decoded grayscale frames at 160x90, compares consecutive frames, and returns frame counts, changed-frame counts, maximum/last change scores, and approximate changed regions. It does not return text or identify UI meaning; use hdmi_screenshot when the AI agent needs a full PNG for visual reasoning. Use this after an input action when timing and repeated screen-change sampling matter.

durationMs.description: How long to monitor the continuous HDMI stream. Default is 5000 milliseconds.

threshold.description: Fraction of 160x90 sample pixels that must differ by at least 16 grayscale levels to count a changed frame. Default is 0.03.

pixelThreshold.description: Per-pixel grayscale difference threshold. Default is 16.

maxEvents.description: Maximum number of changed-region entries to return. Default is 20.

tools.name: hdmi_wait_for_change
tools.description: Capture HDMI frames until the controlled screen objectively changes or the timeout expires. Comparison is model-free grayscale pixel difference over the full screen or an optional source-pixel region. Use after keyboard, mouse, or wheel input when the next action depends on a new screen state. It returns the latest PNG and objective metrics only; it does not perform OCR/VLM or decide what the change means.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum total time to wait. Default is 10000.

intervalMs.description: Time between HDMI samples. Default is 300.

stableSamples.description: Number of consecutive unchanged comparisons required. Default is 3.

screenshotTimeoutMs.description: Maximum wait for each decoded frame. Default is 60000; the first capture in a fresh MCP process takes a few seconds while the device emits its next keyframe to the agent session.

threshold.description: Fraction of pixels in the selected region that must differ by at least 16 grayscale levels. Must be greater than 0; default is 0.03.

tools.name: hdmi_wait_for_stable
tools.description: Capture HDMI frames until the controlled screen remains objectively stable for a configured number of consecutive samples or the timeout expires. Stability is determined by model-free grayscale pixel difference and is useful after a page load or transition before sending the next HID action. It returns the latest PNG and objective metrics only; it does not determine whether the displayed task succeeded.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum total time to wait. Default is 10000.

intervalMs.description: Time between HDMI samples. Default is 300.

stableSamples.description: Number of consecutive unchanged comparisons required. Default is 3.

screenshotTimeoutMs.description: Maximum wait for each decoded frame. Default is 60000; the first capture in a fresh MCP process takes a few seconds while the device emits its next keyframe to the agent session.

threshold.description: Fraction of pixels in the selected region that must differ by at least 16 grayscale levels. Must be greater than 0; default is 0.03.

tools.name: hdmi_wait_for_text
tools.description: Capture HDMI screenshots in a bounded loop, OCR each frame locally, and return as soon as the literal text appears on the controlled screen. Use this to wait for installer pages, boot menus, or login prompts instead of polling hdmi_ocr manually. Matching is whitespace-normalized literal substring matching, optionally case-insensitive (default); there is no regex or semantic understanding, and OCR errors can produce false negatives, so fall back to hdmi_screenshot for visual verification when this reports matched=false.

text.description: Literal text to wait for, for example "Install" or "Press ENTER to continue". Whitespace runs are normalized on both sides.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum total wait time in milliseconds. Default 30000.

intervalMs.description: Delay between capture+OCR samples in milliseconds. Default 1000.

screenshotTimeoutMs.description: Maximum wait for each decoded HDMI frame in milliseconds. Default 15000.

language.description: OCR language data name. Default ARKKVM_OCR_LANG or eng+chi_sim.

tools.name: kvm_atx_power
tools.description: Trigger an ATX power action on the HDMI-connected controlled machine through the ArkKVM ATX control lines: power-short behaves like tapping the power button, power-long like holding it (forced power-off), reset like pressing the reset button. Requires the ATX control extension to be wired to the target machine. This is the supported way to power-cycle the controlled machine so it boots from virtual media during an OS install. It is NOT the ArkKVM device reboot: rebooting the KVM itself would drop this session and unmount state, so that operation is intentionally not exposed here. Every call requires confirm=true.

action.description: ATX action sent to the controlled machine.

confirm.description: Must be explicitly true. Guard against accidental power-off or reset of the controlled machine.

tools.name: kvm_cloud_login
tools.description:
Obtain or clear the cloud web session used by cloud relay mode, without the MCP ever seeing your Google/GitHub credentials. The login UI is the cloud's own page (app origin); this tool runs a one-shot loopback listener on 127.0.0.1 that catches the OIDC redirect and stores the session token.

ACTIONS
- login — requires cloudUrl only (kvm_configure action=set); NO deviceId is needed to log in. Opens the cloud login page in the system browser: it first shows a consent card ("Allow local ArkKVM MCP to access your account") and, after you allow it, the provider buttons. The cloud callback returns a one-time grant code which this tool exchanges (POST /mcp/token) for the dedicated long-lived MCP token — independent of your browser session (no single-session eviction), revocable via the cloud POST /mcp/revoke. Clouds predating the grant flow still redirect with a web-session token; those are captured as kind:'session' with an upgrade hint. Waits (default 300s) for the /ad-login callback, then applies the token and re-enters cloud relay mode. pairing=true is DEPRECATED: it adds cloudDeviceId for a pairing-shaped flow — WARNING: for an already-adopted device this makes the cloud mint a pairing token, which can unbind the device from your account until re-paired. persist=true additionally writes the token (with cloudUrl/cloudDeviceId/cloudDeviceName/kind) to ~/.config/arkkvm-mcp/cloud-token.json (0600) so later MCP processes re-seed from it; env ARKKVM_CLOUD_* always wins over the file. The login-page origin defaults to https://app.arkkvm.com for the global cloud; api.<domain> clouds derive app.<domain>, so api.arkkvm.cn derives https://app.arkkvm.cn for China, while unrelated hosts fall back to the canonical global app origin. If the user specifies an origin — appUrl here, or ARKKVM_CLOUD_APP_URL — it always wins, so pass it whenever the login page lives anywhere else. openBrowser=false returns the login URL instead of opening a browser (the call still waits for the callback). wait=false returns the login URL immediately and applies the token in the background — poll action=status (it then reports the account device list: a single device is auto-picked, with several devices the result carries a nextStep telling you to pick one and set cloudDeviceId); the browser must run on this machine for the 127.0.0.1 callback to arrive. On success without a configured cloudDeviceId the account's device list is fetched: a single device is auto-selected (the result reports it), otherwise the list is returned to pick from.
- devices — requires cloudUrl and a token (from a previous login or kvm_configure). Lists the account's devices (id/name/online) — use this when you don't know your deviceId. When no cloudDeviceId is configured yet and the account has exactly one device, it is auto-selected and the result reports it; with several devices pick one and run kvm_configure action=set cloudDeviceId=<id>. With a cloudDeviceId already configured the list is informational (no re-pick).
- status — cloud mode, token presence, capture time, the resolved cloud device name (cloudDeviceName), pending/background login progress, and token sources (env / persisted file), without revealing the token value. After a background login it also reports the fetched device list (login.devicePickup) and a top-level nextStep: multiple devices → pick the target and run kvm_configure action=set cloudDeviceId=<deviceId>; unclear which → ask the user.
- logout — clears the runtime token and deletes the persisted token file; cloudUrl/cloudDeviceId stay configured.

First-time flow (nothing configured): kvm_configure action=set cloudUrl=<your cloud API> → kvm_cloud_login action=login (persist=true recommended) → kvm_cloud_login action=devices → kvm_configure action=set cloudDeviceId=<picked id> → call any tool.

The agent slot is single-occupancy: a cloud agent session and a device-direct agent session are mutually exclusive (agentSlotOccupied). Headless controllers without any browser — or clouds that keep the browser on their own app after login — should use the manual path instead: sign in, then on the signed-in cloud page run localStorage.getItem('token') in DevTools and call kvm_configure action=set cloudUrl=<api> cloudToken=<value>.

action.description: login starts the loopback OIDC handoff; devices lists the account's devices; status reports cloud session state; logout clears the stored token.

persist.description: login: also persist the captured token to ~/.config/arkkvm-mcp/cloud-token.json (0600) for later MCP processes. Default false. Env ARKKVM_CLOUD_* takes precedence over the file.

appUrl.description: login: cloud app origin hosting the login page. Default https://app.arkkvm.com (global); api.<domain> clouds derive app.<domain> (api.arkkvm.cn → https://app.arkkvm.cn for China), and unrelated hosts fall back to the canonical global app origin; an explicitly specified appUrl — or the ARKKVM_CLOUD_APP_URL env — always wins, so pass it whenever the login page lives anywhere else.

timeoutMs.description: login: how long to wait for the browser callback. Default 300000 (5 minutes), max 600000.

pairing.description: login: DEPRECATED — use the default direct login. Adds the pairing-shaped request (deviceId in the URL). WARNING: for an already cloud-adopted device, a pairing-shaped login makes the cloud mint a pairing token, which can put the device back into re-adoption state (it disappears from the account device list until re-paired). Use only when you intend to (re)pair.

openBrowser.description: login: open the system browser automatically (default true). false just returns loginUrl — the call still waits unless wait=false.

wait.description: login: wait inside this call for the callback (default true). false returns the login URL immediately and applies the token in the background once the browser callback lands; poll action=status.

tools.name: kvm_configure
tools.description: Read or change the KVM connection settings for this MCP process. Settings are held in memory only and this tool never writes them to disk; a restarted MCP server falls back to its environment defaults, except cloud settings (cloudUrl/cloudToken/cloudDeviceId/cloudDeviceName), which additionally re-seed from ~/.config/arkkvm-mcp/cloud-token.json when kvm_cloud_login persist=true wrote it (env ARKKVM_CLOUD_* wins over the file). Exception to memory-only: once a cloudDeviceId is set (and its cloud name resolved), the picked cloudDeviceId/cloudDeviceName are recorded into that token file when it belongs to the same cloud session (same token), so a restarted server keeps the target. Call action=get first when connectivity fails: it reports the current URLs, the cloud device name when one is known (cloud.deviceName, resolved from the account device list), and whether credentials are set, without revealing their values. Device LAN mode (default): set action=set with the device url before any other tool can reach the device. agentCookie and agentCsrfToken are only needed when the device enforces authentication; supply them as the raw cookie value (for example "authTokenAgent=...") and the CSRF token separately. Alternatively, on a password-authenticated device set password once: the MCP then logs in as the agent role automatically and obtains the cookie and CSRF token itself, so agentCookie/agentCsrfToken become unnecessary; an explicitly configured agentCookie still takes precedence. Cloud relay mode: set cloudUrl + cloudDeviceId together, then run kvm_cloud_login action=login (or set cloudToken) to reach an already cloud-adopted device through the ArkKVM cloud without VPN — cloudToken is a cloud access token — normally the dedicated MCP token minted by kvm_cloud_login, or the legacy web-session token (the loginToken from the ad-login redirect) on the manual path — and cloudDeviceId is the device id from the app.arkkvm.com (global) or app.arkkvm.cn (China) device page URL. In cloud mode signaling and ICE/TURN come from the cloud and device-local HTTP status is replaced by cloud-relay info; iceServersJson overrides the cloud-provided TURN servers. Changing any setting closes the current WebRTC session so the next tool call reconnects with the new values. action=reset discards the runtime settings and restores the startup defaults (environment variables, plus the persisted cloud token file when present).

action.description: get reads the current settings; set applies the supplied fields; reset restores the startup defaults (environment variables, plus the persisted cloud token file when present).

url.description: ArkKVM device base URL, for example http://192.168.12.180. This is the KVM device, not the HDMI-connected controlled machine. Used in device LAN mode.

agentCookie.description: Agent-role session cookie sent to the device signaling endpoint. Use the agent cookie only; do not combine it with the user cookie.

agentCsrfToken.description: Agent-role CSRF token paired with agentCookie for authenticated devices.

password.description: ArkKVM device password for devices with password authentication enabled. The MCP logs in as the agent role (POST /auth/login-local) and obtains the session cookie and CSRF token automatically, so agentCookie/agentCsrfToken are no longer needed. Write-only: action=get reports passwordConfigured instead of the value.

iceServersJson.description: ICE servers as a JSON array, for example [{"urls":"stun:127.0.0.1:3478"}]. Omit to let the device signaling response (device mode) or the cloud (cloud mode) supply them. When set in cloud mode it overrides the cloud-provided TURN servers.

cloudUrl.description: ArkKVM cloud API base URL, for example https://api.arkkvm.com (global) or https://api.arkkvm.cn (China). Set it first; the token then comes from kvm_cloud_login action=login (or cloudToken) and cloudDeviceId from the login auto-pick or this setter — all three together switch every tool to cloud relay mode.

cloudToken.description: Cloud token for the relay: prefer the dedicated MCP token minted by kvm_cloud_login (it is what that tool applies); a manually supplied token is the legacy web-session kind (the loginToken from the /ad-login redirect, or the localStorage token on the signed-in cloud page). Write-only: action=get reports tokenConfigured instead of the value.

cloudDeviceId.description: Target device cloud id in cloud relay mode, for example 3dc7f638aa50ce19 — the id in the app.arkkvm.com (global) or app.arkkvm.cn (China) device page URL. Do not know it? Log in first (kvm_cloud_login action=login), then run kvm_cloud_login action=devices to list your devices. The picked id (and its resolved cloud name) is recorded into the persisted token file when it belongs to the same cloud session, so restarts keep the target.

clearAgentCookie.description: Remove the stored agent cookie. Use with action=set.

clearAgentCsrfToken.description: Remove the stored agent CSRF token. Use with action=set.

clearPassword.description: Remove the stored device password. Use with action=set.

clearIceServers.description: Remove the stored ICE servers configuration. Use with action=set.

clearCloudUrl.description: Remove the stored cloud API URL (returns to device LAN mode once all cloud settings are cleared). Use with action=set.

clearCloudToken.description: Remove the stored cloud session token. Use with action=set.

clearCloudDeviceId.description: Remove the stored cloud device id. Use with action=set.

tools.name: kvm_deny_control
tools.description: Withdraw this agent's own pending control request (pauses the task and keeps the current owner). Optional requestId must match the pending arbitration id; omit it to deny the current pending request.

requestId.description: Pending arbitration requestId. Omit to deny the current pending request.

tools.name: kvm_device_settings
tools.description:
Read or change the ArkKVM device hardware and USB-emulation settings shown on the web frontend Device settings page. This configures the KVM device itself, not the HDMI-connected computer.

ACTIONS
- get — no params. Returns guiSettings, usbDevices, usbConfig, and fileTransfer in one call.
- set_backlight — maxBrightness 0-255, dimAfterSeconds / offAfterSeconds 0-86400. At least one required; omitted fields keep their current value (the device replaces the whole backlight setting, so this reads then merges).
- set_display_rotation — rotation '90' (normal) or '270' (inverted).
- set_usb_devices — devices with keyboard, absolute_mouse, relative_mouse, mass_storage, microphone (all required), plus optional network_adapter {enable, adapter_type?, l3_config?}. mass_storage covers both the virtual-media and the file-transfer LUNs. Omitted network_adapter keeps the current device value.
- set_usb_config — usbConfig {vendor_id, product_id ('0x' + 4 hex digits), serial_number, manufacturer, product}: the USB identity the controlled machine sees.
- set_file_transfer — fileTransferEnabled boolean (the virtual USB drive switch).

PRECONDITIONS
- A device or cloud relay target must be configured first (kvm_configure action=set).

SIDE EFFECTS
- set_usb_devices, set_usb_config, and set_file_transfer reboot the USB gadget: the controlled machine re-enumerates its USB devices and HID input can drop for a moment — avoid while driving an installer.
- set_file_transfer to false unmounts the file-transfer volume from the remote USB port first.
- Every set_* action verifies by reading the state back and returns it.

ERRORS (structuredContent carries ok=false with a stable code)
- INVALID_ARGUMENT — required action field missing, or vendor_id/product_id not in 0x0000 form → fix the arguments.
- RPC_DEVICE_ERROR — device rejected the call; deviceCode/deviceData hold the cause.
- DEVICE_NOT_CONFIGURED — no device URL yet → kvm_configure action=set.
- DEVICE_AUTH_REQUIRED — device enforces password auth and the credentials are missing, stale, or wrong (HTTP 401/403) → kvm_configure action=set password=..., or agentCookie + agentCsrfToken.

EXAMPLES
kvm_device_settings action=get
kvm_device_settings action=set_backlight maxBrightness=35 dimAfterSeconds=600

action.description: get reads all settings; the set_* actions apply one setting each and read the state back.

maxBrightness.description: Backlight brightness for set_backlight. 0 turns the display off; the frontend presets are 0, 10, 35, and 64. Omitted fields keep their current value.

dimAfterSeconds.description: Seconds of inactivity before the display dims for set_backlight. 0 disables dimming; frontend presets are 0, 60, 300, 600, 1800, 3600. Omitted fields keep their current value.

offAfterSeconds.description: Seconds of inactivity before the display turns off for set_backlight. 0 disables power-off; frontend presets are 0, 300, 600, 1800, 3600. Omitted fields keep their current value.

rotation.description: Display orientation for set_display_rotation. 90 is normal, 270 is inverted.

mass_storage.description: Mass-storage emulation enabled. One legacy flag: the device applies it to both the virtual-media and the file-transfer mass-storage LUNs.

ip_address.description: Board-side IP on the USB netdev (e.g. 172.16.0.1).

l3_config.description: Board L3 on usb0; omitted fields keep device defaults when enable flips on.

network_adapter.description: USB network adapter. Omitted: keep the device current value (MCP merges before setUsbDevices).

devices.description: Emulated USB device classes for set_usb_devices. Five HID/storage/mic flags are required; network_adapter is optional and merged from current state when omitted. Reboots the USB gadget.

serial_number.description: USB serial number string reported to the controlled machine.

manufacturer.description: USB manufacturer string reported to the controlled machine.

product.description: USB product string reported to the controlled machine.

usbConfig.description: USB identifier strings for set_usb_config, as reported to the controlled machine. Reboots the USB gadget, so the target sees a new USB device.

fileTransferEnabled.description: File-transfer (virtual USB drive) switch for set_file_transfer. Reboots the mass-storage gadget; disabling it first unmounts the volume from the remote USB port.

timeoutMs.description: RPC timeout in milliseconds per call. Default 30000; setUsbDevices applies after a USB gadget restart and may need more.

tools.name: kvm_get_control
tools.description: Read who currently holds ArkKVM HID control (user vs agent) and whether a controlConflict arbitration is pending. Use this before keyboard/mouse when a human may be sharing the device, and after controlConflict/controlChanged events.

tools.name: kvm_health_snapshot
tools.description: Collect a one-shot diagnostic snapshot of the ArkKVM device by running a fixed set of read-only checks in parallel: HTTP device status plus device ID, video state, USB state and device flags, virtual media state and list, file transfer state, current version, update status, network state, storage space/details/files, mass storage mode, and keyboard layout. In cloud relay mode this also includes cloudConfig (relay target, token presence and age) and cloudIceServers (cloud-provided ICE/TURN availability, exercising the cloud API auth path). Individual check failures do not abort the snapshot; each check reports ok/result or ok=false/error. Use this before starting an OS install flow to confirm the device, HDMI video, and virtual media are ready.

timeoutMs.description: Total budget for all checks in milliseconds. Default 30000.

tools.name: kvm_ip_forward_host
tools.description: Forward a local TCP/UDP port on the controller to an explicit host reachable from the ArkKVM device (board LAN/VLAN/Tailscale, etc.). Use directly ONLY when the user explicitly wants a target that is NOT the HDMI-controlled machine. For the controlled machine, prefer kvm_ip_forward_usb first; use this tool as fallback only after user confirmation that host is the controlled-machine address. Actions: open, status, close.

action.description: open starts a local listener; status/close need sessionId

sessionId.description: Session ID from open; required for status/close

host.description: Host reachable from the KVM device. Required for open.

localPort.description: Local listen port; 0 or omit for ephemeral.

tools.name: kvm_ip_forward_usb
tools.description: Forward a local TCP/UDP port on the controller to the HDMI-controlled machine through ArkKVM USB networking. Preferred path for the controlled host: do NOT pass a host IP — the device resolves the peer from its USB DHCP lease. Prerequisites: enable the USB network adapter on the device. On failure, tell the user they can enable USB network; using kvm_ip_forward_host as fallback requires explicit user confirmation that the host is the controlled machine. Actions: open (returns localHost/localPort), status, close. After open, use standard clients against 127.0.0.1:localPort (ssh, curl, etc.).

action.description: open starts a local listener; status/close need sessionId

sessionId.description: Session ID from open; required for status/close

port.description: Target port on the controlled machine. Required for open.

localPort.description: Local listen port; 0 or omit for ephemeral.

tools.name: kvm_key_sequence
tools.description: Send a sequence of USB HID keyboard chords to the HDMI-connected controlled machine through ArkKVM, using named keys instead of raw usage IDs. Each step holds one key combination (up to six keys plus modifiers), sends the key-down report, waits holdMs, and always sends the release report before continuing. This is the preferred typing tool for installer wizards: use steps like [{keys:["enter"]}], [{keys:["d","e","l"],modifiers:[]}], or one chord step [{keys:["delete"],modifiers:["ctrl","alt"]}]. Key tokens are interpreted by the target machine own OS keyboard layout. For raw HID usage IDs use kvm_keyboard instead.

keys.description: Named keys pressed together in this step. Tokens: a-z, 0-9, enter, esc, backspace, tab, space, minus, equal, leftbracket, rightbracket, backslash, semicolon, quote, backquote, comma, dot, slash, capslock, f1..f12, printscreen, scrolllock, pause, insert, home, pageup, delete, end, pagedown, right, left, down, up, numlock.

modifiers.description: Modifier names held during this step: ctrl, shift, alt, gui. Aliases: control, option, win, windows, cmd, command, super, meta. On a Windows target the Windows key is gui.

holdMs.description: How long this step keys are held before the release report. Overrides the tool-level holdMs for this step.

delayAfterMs.description: Extra pause after this step release before the next step. Overrides the tool-level delayAfterMs for this step.

steps.description: Ordered keyboard steps. One entry per key press or chord; sequences of entries type one key after another.

holdMs.description: Default milliseconds each step keys are held before release. Default 60.

delayAfterMs.description: Default pause between steps after the release report. Default 60.

tools.name: kvm_keyboard
tools.description: Send one USB HID keyboard report to the HDMI-connected controlled machine through the ArkKVM USB connection. This accepts HID usage IDs, not text, Unicode characters, browser key names, or macOS key codes. The target machine interprets the report according to its own OS and keyboard layout. keys contains up to six simultaneously pressed non-modifier HID usage IDs; modifier is an 8-bit bitmask. For a normal key press send a key-down report, wait briefly if needed, then send a release report with keys all zero and modifier zero. For a shortcut, send the modifier and key together, then always release all keys. Common modifier bits: Left Ctrl=0x01, Left Shift=0x02, Left Alt=0x04, Left GUI/Windows/Command=0x08, Right Ctrl=0x10, Right Shift=0x20, Right Alt=0x40, Right GUI=0x80. On a Windows target, use Left GUI (0x08) for the Windows key even when the controller runs macOS; the controller platform must not be substituted for the target platform. Platform-specific shortcut mapping is not implemented yet.

keys.description: Up to six USB HID usage IDs for simultaneously pressed non-modifier keys. Example: Keyboard A is 0x04; Enter is 0x28; the Windows/GUI key is a modifier and belongs in modifier, not keys. Use [] or [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] for release.

modifier.description: USB HID modifier bitmask. Combine bits with bitwise OR: Left Ctrl 0x01, Left Shift 0x02, Left Alt 0x04, Left GUI/Windows/Command 0x08, Right Ctrl 0x10, Right Shift 0x20, Right Alt/AltGr 0x40, Right GUI 0x80. Use 0 when no modifier is pressed.

tools.name: kvm_mouse
tools.description: Send one USB HID mouse report to the HDMI-connected controlled machine through ArkKVM. Use absolute mode when the screen coordinate is known or when first placing the pointer; use relative mode for small movement or dragging. Absolute coordinates use the HID range 0..32767 in both axes, where (0,0) is the top-left and (16384,16384) is approximately the center. buttons is a held-button bitmask: Left=1, Right=2, Middle=4. A click requires separate reports with the same position: buttons=1, then buttons=0. Always release buttons after a click or drag. This tool moves/clicks the target pointer; it does not provide screen content or verify that the pointer landed on a visible control. For scrolling, first move to the scrollable target and click if focus is needed, then call kvm_wheel.

mode.description: Input mode. Use absolute for screen placement/clicking; use relative for movement by dx/dy or dragging.

x.description: Absolute horizontal HID coordinate, 0..32767 from left to right. Required when mode is absolute; ignored in relative mode.

y.description: Absolute vertical HID coordinate, 0..32767 from top to bottom. Required when mode is absolute; ignored in relative mode.

dx.description: Relative horizontal movement for one HID report, -128..127. Required when mode is relative; ignored in absolute mode.

dy.description: Relative vertical movement for one HID report, -128..127. Required when mode is relative; ignored in absolute mode.

buttons.description: Held mouse-button bitmask: Left=1, Right=2, Middle=4. Use 0 for movement without a held button and for button release.

tools.name: kvm_release_control
tools.description: Release HID control held by this agent so a connected human (or vacant lease) can take it. Prefer this when the agent finishes a task and wants to return control.

tools.name: kvm_request_control
tools.description: Ask the ArkKVM device for HID control for this agent session. If a human already holds control, the device starts arbitration: the human sees a WebUI popup and may hand over control, otherwise control transfers automatically after 120s of silence. The requester can never grant its own request (the device refuses with controlDenied). If this agent already owns control, returns the current state. On conflict, pause the task and poll kvm_get_control until owner=agent.

tools.name: kvm_rpc
tools.description:
Call one allowlisted, read-only ArkKVM device JSON-RPC method through the WebRTC rpc DataChannel. This queries the KVM device control plane, not the HDMI-connected computer; it is not a shell and cannot run commands such as ls, dir, PowerShell, or cmd on the controlled machine. Write operations live in dedicated tools: kvm_device_settings, kvm_virtual_media, kvm_virtual_usb, kvm_storage_upload, kvm_storage_delete, kvm_atx_power.

ALLOWED METHODS (read-only; anything else is rejected as RPC_METHOD_NOT_EXPOSED)
- identity/version: ping, getDeviceID, getCurrentVersion, getUpdateStatus, getTLSState
- video/input: getVideoState, getKeyboardLedState, getKeyboardLayout, getKeyboardMacros, getSerialSettings
- network: getNetworkState, getNetworkSettings, getCloudState
- storage/media: getStorageSpace, getStorageDetails, listStorageFiles, getFtStorageDetails, ftListFile, getVirtualMediaState, getVirtualMediaList, getMassStorageMode, getFileTransferState
- usb: getUSBState, getUsbDevices, getUsbConfig
- settings: getGuiSettings, getFileTransfer, getDevModeState

TYPICAL ORDER
1. device_status first when connectivity is uncertain.
2. kvm_rpc with the exact method name; pass params only for methods that take them (most take none).

ERRORS (structuredContent carries ok=false with a stable code)
- RPC_METHOD_NOT_EXPOSED — method missing from the list above → use a dedicated tool or report unsupported.
- RPC_DEVICE_ERROR — device rejected the call; deviceCode/deviceData hold its error and cause.
- RPC_TIMEOUT — no response within timeoutMs → retry with a larger timeoutMs.
- DEVICE_NOT_CONFIGURED — no device URL yet → kvm_configure action=set.
- DEVICE_AUTH_REQUIRED — device enforces password auth and the credentials are missing, stale, or wrong (HTTP 401/403) → kvm_configure action=set password=..., or agentCookie + agentCsrfToken.

EXAMPLE
kvm_rpc method=getGuiSettings → {method, result:{max_brightness, dim_after, off_after, rotation}}

method.description: Exact allowlisted ArkKVM RPC method name, for example ping or getUSBState. This is not a target-machine shell command.

params.description: JSON object containing parameters for the selected allowlisted RPC method. Omit when the method takes no parameters.

timeoutMs.description: RPC response timeout in milliseconds. Default is 30000.

tools.name: kvm_storage_delete
tools.description: Delete one file from the ArkKVM device storage. This is destructive and always requires confirm=true. destination=storage removes an image from the virtual-media storage folder (as listed by kvm_rpc listStorageFiles); deleting a missing storage file is an idempotent success. destination=fileTransfer removes one regular file from the file-transfer volume (as listed by kvm_virtual_usb action=list) and requires that volume to be mounted. Directories are not deleted by this tool. A storage image that is currently mounted is rejected: unmount it with kvm_virtual_media action=unmount first, then delete it.

destination.description: storage (default) = virtual-media images folder; fileTransfer = virtual USB drive volume.

filename.description: Storage filename to delete for destination=storage. No path separators.

path.description: File path relative to the file-transfer volume root for destination=fileTransfer, for example "/docs/report.pdf". Must name a regular file, not a directory or the volume root.

confirm.description: Must be explicitly true. Deletion cannot be undone.

tools.name: kvm_storage_upload
tools.description:
Upload a controller-local file to the ArkKVM device over the WebRTC upload DataChannel. localPath is read on the machine running this MCP server.

DESTINATIONS
- storage (default) — device images folder for virtual media ISOs. Follow up with kvm_virtual_media action=mount_storage (OS-install flow); list with kvm_rpc listStorageFiles.
- fileTransfer — the virtual USB drive volume for ordinary files the controlled machine should see. Follow up with kvm_virtual_usb action=mount (when not mounted) and verify with kvm_virtual_usb action=list. remotePath selects the target directory (default '/').

PRECONDITIONS
- fileTransfer requires the volume to be mounted on the device: kvm_virtual_usb action=state reports the mount target, and when it is null run kvm_virtual_usb action=mount first. Note that action=unmount unmounts the filesystem on the device itself and blocks uploads and listings until it is mounted again.
- fileTransfer refuses an existing target file: pick another remoteFilename or delete the existing one with kvm_storage_delete.

TYPICAL ORDER (fileTransfer)
1. kvm_virtual_usb action=state — mount when the target is null.
2. kvm_storage_upload destination=fileTransfer localPath=... remotePath=/ remoteFilename=...
3. kvm_virtual_usb action=list path=<remotePath> — confirm the file is there.

RESUME
- Interrupted uploads keep partial data server-side; rerunning the same call resumes from the acknowledged byte offset (both destinations).

ERRORS (structuredContent carries ok=false with a stable code)
- FT_VOLUME_NOT_MOUNTED — fileTransfer volume unmounted → kvm_virtual_usb action=mount (or kvm_device_settings action=set_file_transfer).
- FT_FILE_EXISTS — target name already taken → change remoteFilename or delete the existing file with kvm_storage_delete.
- UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE — connection ended before the last byte → rerun the same call to resume.
- SOURCE_FILE_INVALID — localPath missing, not a regular file, empty, or over the size limit.
- DEVICE_NOT_CONFIGURED — no device URL yet → kvm_configure action=set.
- DEVICE_AUTH_REQUIRED — device enforces password auth and the credentials are missing, stale, or wrong (HTTP 401/403) → kvm_configure action=set password=..., or agentCookie + agentCsrfToken.

EXAMPLE
kvm_storage_upload destination=fileTransfer localPath=/tmp/report.pdf remotePath=/ remoteFilename=report.pdf

localPath.description: Absolute or relative path of the file on the controller machine. Directories and special files are rejected.

destination.description: storage (default) = device images folder for virtual media ISOs (use with kvm_virtual_media); fileTransfer = the virtual USB drive volume for ordinary files (use with kvm_virtual_usb).

remoteFilename.description: Filename inside the destination. Defaults to the local file basename. No path separators.

remotePath.description: Directory on the file-transfer volume for destination=fileTransfer, for example "/" or "/docs". Default "/". Ignored for destination=storage.

timeoutMs.description: Total upload budget in milliseconds. Default 1800000 (30 minutes).

tools.name: kvm_virtual_media
tools.description: Inspect and control the ArkKVM virtual media (virtual CD-ROM / disk) that is exposed to the HDMI-connected controlled machine over USB. Actions: state reads the current mount (null when nothing is mounted); list reads the saved URL presets; mount_url streams an image over HTTP(S) from a Range-request-capable server (the device mounts it without storing it); mount_storage mounts a file previously uploaded into device storage with kvm_storage_upload; unmount detaches the current media. Mount mode CDROM suits OS installer ISOs. Only one virtual media can be mounted at a time; pass forceUnmount=true to replace an existing mount. After mounting for an install, boot or reboot the controlled machine with kvm_atx_power.

url.description: http(s) image URL for mount_url. The remote server must support Range requests (206 responses).

filename.description: Storage filename for mount_storage, as listed by kvm_health_snapshot listStorageFiles. No path separators.

mode.description: Mount mode. CDROM for installer ISOs, DISK for raw disk images. Default CDROM.

forceUnmount.description: Unmount an already mounted media before mounting. Default false; mounting over an existing media then fails.

tools.name: kvm_virtual_usb
tools.description: Inspect and expose the ArkKVM file-transfer (virtual USB drive) filesystem to the HDMI-connected controlled machine. Actions: state reads the current file-transfer mount target (null when the feature is disabled); list lists files in one directory of the device file-transfer volume (the volume mounted at /mnt/ft_disk, including any .iso or disk images placed there); mount exposes the whole file-transfer volume to the controlled machine (target Kvm) or to the remote USB port (target RemoteUsb) as a USB mass-storage disk; unmount detaches it. Files on this volume are exposed as files on a USB disk, which the controlled machine can read after boot; booting an installer requires the firmware to support USB boot, unlike the virtual CD-ROM provided by kvm_virtual_media.

path.description: Directory to list, relative to the volume root, for action=list. Default "/". No ".." components.

target.description: Exposure target for action=mount. Kvm exposes the volume to the HDMI-controlled machine as a USB disk. Default Kvm.

tools.name: kvm_wheel
tools.description: Send one USB HID mouse-wheel report through ArkKVM to the controlled machine. The wheel acts at the target machine current pointer position, so move the pointer over a scrollable control first; if the application needs focus, click at that position and release the button before scrolling. wheelY is a signed HID tick, normally -1 for one notch down and +1 for one notch up. Repeat this tool call for a larger scroll; do not pass browser pixel deltas such as 100 as one report. wheelX is optional horizontal scrolling and defaults to 0. The result confirms that the report was sent, not that a particular page visibly scrolled.

wheelY.description: Vertical wheel movement in signed HID ticks. Use -1 for one notch down, +1 for one notch up; repeat calls for more scrolling. Use 0 when only horizontal scrolling is required.

wheelX.description: Optional horizontal wheel movement in signed HID ticks. Defaults to 0.
